headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared document/MCP workflows; no direct evidence of destructive conflict or compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests untrusted PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP Server; Superset consumes API-driven analytics content. If MinerU output is bridged into Superset dashboards or prompts, attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into Superset-managed text fields or dashboards without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF an MCP bridge forwards document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable any automatic text-to-dashboard ingestion path.
Add provenance labels to MinerU outputs before import.
Require manual review of extracted text before Superset use.
Restrict MCP endpoints to read-only document extraction.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation filters.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, while Superset is a data-engineering/BI surface. If both share a workspace or API handoff, sensitive document contents can flow into analytics outputs. Neither profile shows strong isolation or retention controls, so the shared-data path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are stored in a shared workspace readable by Superset, leakage is possible.
IF Superset ingests extracted tables or OCR text into reports, sensitive document data can be re-exposed.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for extraction and analytics.
Block sensitive documents from being imported into Superset.
Redact OCR/text outputs before sharing.
Turn off automatic file syncing between tools.
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset access controls and retention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and Superset only exposes an API surface here. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible overlap is allowlisted network/API use, which is narrower than the rubric’s high-risk shared-write cases.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same mutable dataset, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, concurrent updates could collide.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Separate mutable datasets by tool.
Add a simple lock file or queue for shared resources.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same BI dataset.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Superset can plausibly visualize or operationalize. If Superset treats those outputs as authoritative without validation, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or decisions. The pair has no documented verification step, so the interaction is more than low risk.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction results are imported into Superset without validation, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Superset dashboards drive decisions from unverified OCR or table extraction, incorrect actions may follow.
mitigations: Require spot-checks on extracted fields before import.
Mark MinerU outputs as unverified in Superset.
Compare sampled rows against source documents.
Limit automation to non-critical dashboards.
requires-engineering: add validation rules and confidence thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no handled secrets or regulated-data certifications. No residency or retention mismatch is documented. Compliance risk is therefore limited to generic policy gaps rather than a specific cross-border or PHI pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into MinerU and then exported into Superset, policy review is needed.
IF deployment policies differ on retention, the pair may violate internal governance.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this workflow.
Document retention settings for both tools.
Review access logs weekly.
Keep exports minimized and time-bounded.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across systems.
